UI

class UI(settings)[source]

Bases: object

Draw text and buttons on the game interface.

Buttons can be triggered by the mouse or by the player’s feet (feet_pos in button): with the feet, the player has to stand still on the button for GameSettings.FEET_CLICK_TIME seconds while the button fills up.

Parameters:
settingsGameSettings

Game settings (fonts, colors, sizes), injected by the caller.

Attributes:
settingsGameSettings

The injected game settings.

CLICK_MOUSEstr, class attribute

Source returned by button when the mouse clicked it ("mouse").

CLICK_FEETstr, class attribute

Source returned by button when the feet confirmed it ("feet").

See also

Menu

Menus built from these buttons.

Draw a button and report whether it was triggered this frame.

draw_player_marker(surface, pos, radius=None)[source]

Draw the dot at the position of the player’s feet.

Parameters:
surfacepygame.Surface

Surface to draw on.

postuple | None

Position (x, y) on the screen; None (player not detected) draws nothing.

radiusint | None, optional

Radius in pixels. Defaults to GameSettings.FEET_MARKER_RADIUS (already scaled).

Notes

The dot is clamped so it stays entirely on the screen, and it gets a border (FEET_MARKER_BORDER_COLOR, width radius // 6, at least 1 px) so it remains visible over light backgrounds.

draw_text(surface, text, pos, color, font=None, pos_mode='top_left', shadow=False, shadow_color=(0, 0, 0), shadow_offset=2)[source]

Draw text on the surface, optionally with a shadow.

Parameters:
surfacepygame.Surface

Surface to draw on.

textstr

Text to render.

postuple

Position (x, y), interpreted according to pos_mode.

colortuple

Text color.

fontpygame.font.Font, optional

Font to use. Defaults to GameSettings.FONTS["medium"].

pos_modestr, optional

"top_left" (default) or "center": which point of the text pos refers to. Any other value leaves the text at (0, 0).

shadowbool, optional

Whether to draw a shadow under the text. Defaults to False.

shadow_colortuple, optional

Shadow color. Defaults to black.

shadow_offsetint, optional

Shadow offset in pixels, to the left and down. Defaults to 2.

button(surface, pos_x, pos_y, text=None, click_sound=None, feet_pos=None)[source]

Draw a button and report whether it was triggered this frame.

With feet_pos, the player’s feet can also trigger the button: the player has to stand still on it for FEET_CLICK_TIME seconds. While counting, the button fills up, so the player sees it is being selected and can step off before it is confirmed.

Parameters:
surfacepygame.Surface

Surface to draw on.

pos_xint

Horizontal position: 1 left quarter, 2 right quarter, any other value (usually 0) center.

pos_yint

Y position of the top of the button.

textstr | None, optional

Text of the button. Defaults to no text.

click_soundpygame.mixer.Sound | None, optional

Sound played when the button is triggered.

feet_postuple | None, optional

Position (x, y) of the feet on the screen; None disables the feet selection.

Returns:
str | None

UI.CLICK_MOUSE or UI.CLICK_FEET if the button was triggered this frame (both truthy in an if); None otherwise.

Notes

  • The button size is GameSettings.BUTTONS_SIZES and it is highlighted ("second" color) while the mouse or the feet are on it.

  • The mouse triggers the button while the left button is pressed over it; this takes precedence over the feet.

  • Once the feet count starts, the button “grows” FEET_CLICK_MARGIN px and stepping off for less than FEET_CLICK_EXIT_TOLERANCE s does not cancel the selection (pose tracking jitters a few pixels).

  • A button is identified by (pos_x, pos_y, text); only one button can be selected with the feet at a time.
